item.title: Fast Dynamic Re‐Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode‐Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
item.description:
افزودن دیکلرواتان به الکترولیت AlCl3/EMIC تعادل گونه‌های کلروآلومینات را تسریع کرده و پایداری فصل مشترک الکترود-الکترولیت و آند آلومینیم را در باتری یون آلومینیم بهبود می‌دهد.
Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using a low-polarity, small-molecule moderator (dichloroethane) to reconfigure the interionic interaction network in AlCl₃/EMIC electrolyte, accelerating chloroaluminate speciation re-equilibration and suppressing charge-carrier depletion. This enables reversible AlCl₄⁻/Al₂Cl₇⁻ conversion, dendrite suppression, and unprecedented Al anode stability, boosting graphite-cathode capacity 120.7% (92→203 mAh g⁻¹) over 7000 cycles—establishing a dynamic speciation regulation principle for long-life aluminum-ion batteries.
🏷 aluminum-ion battery · chloroaluminate speciation · ionic liquid electrolyte · dichloroethane moderator · Al anode stability

Advanced Energy Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Non-stoichiometric tunnel-structured Mo5O14 enables reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition or lattice strain, overcoming proton-induced instability in aqueous proton batteries. It delivers 271 mAh g−1, ultrahigh-rate capability (300 A g−1), and 310,000-cycle stability, plus a full cell with 73.3 Wh kg−1 and flexible micro-cells, establishing phase-stable non-stoichiometric oxides as a design strategy for durable proton storage.
🏷 proton battery · molybdenum oxide · tunnel structure · H3O+ intercalation · phase stability

item.title: Engineering Energy‐Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
item.description:

Advanced Energy Materials | ⭐ Review
💡 This Review uniquely bridges ALD/MLD surface chemistry with process design for energy-storage interfaces, addressing complex real-world substrates beyond ideal oxides. Its chemistry–process–structure–function framework links precursor pathways and nucleation to ionic transport, kinetics, and mechanical stability across Li and beyond-Li systems, while assessing scalability and validation. Six design rules presented as a decision flow translate mechanistic insight into practical interface engineering guidance.

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an anode-centric strategy using a Na-rich nanoalloy (NaxSn) to simultaneously suppress cation and anion crosstalk via ultrafast kinetics (raising the Damköhler number) and an ultrathin Na2O-rich SEI that physically blocks crossover. This enables high-efficiency FeF2 and S/C full cells with extreme rate capability and 1000-cycle pouch-cell stability, advancing sustainable high-energy batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in extending d-band center theory to a high-entropy complementary model, using multi-metal d-band alignment to match sulfur species' HOMO/LUMO and balance electron transfer. This enables a closed-loop capture-conversion-desorption pathway that suppresses shuttle effects, yielding high-entropy selenide catalysts with superior cycle stability and rate performance in Li–S batteries.

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in a multifunctional polymeric layer with amide and imidazolium groups creating confined-water domains where water acts as a transient coordination bridge for partially desolvated Zn²⁺ transport while its mobility is restricted. This simultaneously boosts single-ion conductivity 6.55-fold and cuts hydrogen evolution 79.1%, enabling 2200 h Zn//Zn cycling and 4000-cycle Zn–I₂ cells with >85% retention—a robust interfacial strategy for durable aqueous ZIBs.
